purpose: Teach: いやー/片方/あちら/情けない/火事/外食/つまみ/みかん

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いやー、ばあさん、若い頃、お父さん、よく頑張ったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, Gran — your father worked so hard. You remember that, don't you? I'm being serious.
lines.style: Warm nostalgia with a slight catch in the voice. Opening words pull back in time. Conversational pace, gentle. The final assertion lands softly but with real sincerity — he wants her to know he means it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、お父さんの、絶対、靴下の、絶対、片方、絶対、よく失くしてたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh yes. When your grandfather was young, your father — he was always losing one sock. Always just one. You remember that, don't you dear? I really do mean it.
lines.style: Amused affection threading through. She's reliving the small absurdity of it. Warm, unhurried pace. Slight skip of laughter in the middle. The ending is tender but has weight — she's confirming the memory with him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、あちら、絶対、のおうち、絶対、よく訪ねたわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, Gran — we used to visit that house nearby so often. You remember, don't you? I'm serious.
lines.style: Reflective, almost dreamy opening. His voice softens on the memory. Measured pace, no rush. Slight lingering on 'often.' The closing assertion is quiet but grounded.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、お給料、絶対、減って、絶対、情けない、絶対、なって、絶対、おっしゃってたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Back then, when your grandfather was young — his salary had gone down, and he felt so ashamed about it. You remember how he said that, don't you dear? I'm serious about that.
lines.style: Her tone shifts toward something more tender and protective. She's naming something vulnerable he carried. Slower pace here, deliberate. She's not dwelling, but not rushing either. The ending voice softens further — this memory matters.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、近所で、絶対、火事、絶対、あった日、絶対、お父さん、絶対、駆け付けたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, Gran — there was a fire nearby one day, and your father rushed right out to help. You remember that, don't you? I'm being serious.
lines.style: Pride edges into the nostalgia now. Voice rises slightly on 'rushed.' Quickens just a touch on the memory of action. Then settles back into sincerity. The final words carry weight — he wants her to know he admires it still.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、結婚記念日、絶対、外食、絶対、連れて行ってくれたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When your grandfather was young, on our anniversary he'd take me out to eat. He really did. You remember that, don't you dear? I'm telling you true.
lines.style: Pure tenderness now. Her voice curves up slightly with the warmth of the memory. Almost shy about naming it. Gentle pace, savoring the detail. The close is intimate — she's sharing something precious with him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、お父さんに、絶対、お酒の、絶対、つまみ、絶対、用意してくれたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, Gran — your father, he'd prepare little snacks for my sake. Good snacks. You remember that, don't you? I mean it.
lines.style: Soft gratitude in the voice. Opens with a slight smile. Warm and unhurried. Lingers gently on the care of the gesture. The assertion at the end is quiet, almost humble — these small kindnesses still matter to him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、お庭で、絶対、みかん、絶対、を、絶対、育てたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When your grandfather was young, he grew mandarin oranges in the garden. Right there. You remember that, don't you dear? I really do remember.
lines.style: Quiet contentment. She's seeing the garden in her mind. Slow, peaceful pace. Slight warmth on 'mandarin oranges' — specificity brings it alive. The ending is gentle affirmation — the memory is real, it's lived.
